questions.question: What is the time complexity of searching an element in an unsorted array of size N?
questions.explanation: In an unsorted array, we may need to inspect all N elements in the worst case (Linear Search).

questions.question: Which asymptotic notation gives the tightest bound for both upper and lower limits?
questions.explanation: Big-Theta (Θ) specifies both asymptotic upper and lower bounds simultaneously.

questions.question: Why does accessing an element in an array have O(1) time complexity?
options: Because elements are stored with hash keys
Because memory is contiguous and index offset can be directly calculated
Because compiler caches all values in registers
Because arrays use binary search internally
questions.explanation: Base address + index * element_size gives immediate memory address in O(1).

questions.question: What is the time complexity to insert a new node at the head of a Singly Linked List?
questions.explanation: Inserting at the head only requires updating the new node's next pointer and head pointer in O(1).

questions.question: Which data structure is fundamentally used for function call stacks during recursion?
questions.explanation: The call stack operates under Last-In First-Out (LIFO) semantics.

questions.question: What happens if a recursive function does not have a proper base case?
options: Stack Overflow error due to infinite recursive calls
questions.explanation: Without a base termination condition, activation records exhaust the call stack limit.

questions.question: Inorder traversal of a Binary Search Tree (BST) visits nodes in which order?
questions.explanation: Inorder traversal (Left, Root, Right) always outputs values of a BST in ascending order.

questions.question: What is the worst-case search time complexity in a skewed Binary Search Tree of N nodes?
questions.explanation: A skewed BST degrades to a linked list, resulting in O(N) linear search time.

questions.question: What is the time complexity to extract the minimum element from a Binary Min-Heap of size N?
questions.explanation: Extracting root is O(1), but restoring min-heap property via heapify-down takes O(log N).

questions.question: What is the space complexity of storing a sparse graph with V vertices and E edges using an Adjacency List?
questions.explanation: Adjacency list stores V list headers and 2E (or E) total node elements: O(V + E).

questions.question: Which data structure is essential to implement Breadth-First Search (BFS) on a graph?
questions.explanation: BFS explores neighbors level-by-level using a First-In First-Out Queue.

questions.question: Which algorithm computes topological ordering of a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) using in-degrees?
questions.explanation: Kahn's algorithm repeatedly removes vertices with 0 in-degree using a queue.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of Dijkstra's Shortest Path algorithm implemented with a Min-Heap priority queue?
questions.explanation: Using binary heap priority queue, edge relaxations and vertex extractions take O((V + E) log V).

questions.question: Which disjoint-set optimizations achieve near O(1) amortized time per operation in Kruskal's algorithm?
options: Path compression and Union by Rank/Size
questions.explanation: Path compression + Union by rank achieves inverse Ackermann α(N) amortized time.

questions.question: What are the two key properties required to apply Dynamic Programming?
options: Divide and Conquer without state caching
questions.explanation: Dynamic Programming requires optimal solutions from subproblems (optimal substructure) and redundant subproblems (overlapping).

questions.question: What is the time complexity of the Floyd-Warshall all-pairs shortest path algorithm on V vertices?
questions.explanation: Floyd-Warshall uses 3 nested loops over all vertices: O(V^3).
